data.claim: build_parser() attaches a resolvable completion kind to every argument action: choices -> enum, an id-like name or an id positional of a record verb -> id:<kind>, a path name/metavar -> path/dir, else none. An argument that is id-like or has a closed value set yet resolves to none fails a ratchet test unless explicitly exempt.
data.falsifier: A probe over build_parser() shows a choices-bearing or id-named action that resolves to none with no exemption, or an action whose kind changes without any code change.
data.mechanism: kinds.infer() is a pure stdlib function on (dest, choices, metavar, positional, record_kind). Param.complete declares, add_to attaches the resolved kind onto the argparse action, hand-written add_argument calls use a one-line helper. completion_exemptions.py lists any argument that must not complete, with a reason.
data.probe: python3 -c: walk build_parser(), count actions; enumerate options/positionals with choices and their dests/metavars; count id-like dests (item/phase/bug/lesson/.../id) and path/dir metavars.
data.probe_output: options 2109, positionals 136, subparsers 28; 19 options with choices (--kind, --outcome, --status, --result, --sort, --mode, --bump, --launch, --cwd, --reviewer, --applies-to, --into, --format, --at, ...); 11 positionals with choices; metavars ID x37, DIR x3, NAME x2. A deterministic name->kind table covers every entry; none requires per-argument code.
data.question: Can every ddflow argument's shell-completion value kind be declared on the argument (Param.complete) and inferred from its own name/choices/type, so a new command, option, choice or record kind needs no per-argument completion code, and a forgotten declaration is caught by a ratchet instead of silently offering nothing?

evidence.note: R-completion-declare-kind CONFIRMED: probe over build_parser() shows 2109 options/136 positionals/28 subparsers; 19 options and 11 positionals carry choices (--kind/--outcome/--status/--result/--sort/--mode/...), metavars ID x37/DIR x3; the name->kind inference table (choices->enum, id-like name->id:<kind>, path/dir metavar->path/dir) decides every argument deterministically from its own action, no per-argument code. Falsifier (a choices/id-like action resolving to none without exemption) is exactly what the ratchet asserts against.

chunk_findings.detail: `metavar="PATH"` is classified as a directory. `DIR_METAVARS` is `{"DIR", "PATH"}` and that branch returns `"dir"` before `FILE` is considered, and nothing maps `PATH` to `"path"`. Given `infer("spec", metavar="PATH")` the result is `"dir"`, so TAB only offers directories and a file-valued `--spec PATH` cannot be completed. The kind vocabulary treats `"path"` as file paths and the infer docstring claims `DIR`/`PATH`/`FILE` resolve to dir/path; this input gets the wrong one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/kinds.py:infer

chunk_findings.detail: Path inference never sees the argument type, despite the change requiring paths to come from the type. `infer` only takes name, choices, metavar, positional, and record kind. Given an action `add_argument("--config", type=pathlib.Path)` (dest `config`, metavar defaulting to `CONFIG`, no choices), `infer("config")` returns `"none"`, so the path is free text and will not complete. Named exceptions in `PATH_NAMES`/`DIR_NAMES` do not cover ordinary typed path parameters.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/kinds.py:infer

chunk_findings.detail: The loop asserts `kind == "enum"` whenever `action.choices is not None`, but `_resolve` returns a declared `complete` before inference. Intent allows `complete` of `phase`, `gate`, `agent`, `state`, `path`, `dir`, or `none` even when choices are set, and "choices -> enum" applies only when complete is unset. Given an action with `choices=("open", "closed")` and `complete="state"`, `_resolve` returns `"state"` and the assertion fails, so a correct future declaration is rejected by CI.

chunk_findings.detail: The `state` branch ignores `prefix`, contradicting the function’s contract that it returns “Candidates for ``prefix``”. For an index whose `CI.states(index=index)` returns, say, `["open", "done"]`, a call like `V.complete("state", "do", index=...)` returns `["open", "done"]` rather than only `["done"]`. The completion engine may then offer or insert a non-matching state. The added test only exercises `V.complete("state", "", index=index)`, so it does not catch the missing prefix filter.

chunk_findings.detail: `path` and `dir` are documented as completion kinds, and the stated intent requires path completion for `--globs` and `--repo`, but `complete` falls through to `return []` for them. Given a completion request for kind `path` with prefix `src/` (or kind `dir` with prefix `dd/`), this kind-to-source table produces no candidates, so the promised path/directory completion is not implemented here; the test `test_none_path_dir_offer_nothing` explicitly locks in the empty result.

The completion engine may then offer or insert a non-matching state. The added test only exercises `V.complete("state", "", index=index)`, so it does not catch the missing prefix filter.

chunk_findings.detail: `path` and `dir` are documented as completion kinds, and the stated intent requires path completion for `--globs` and `--repo`, but `complete` falls through to `return []` for them. Given a completion request for kind `path` with prefix `src/` (or kind `dir` with prefix `dd/`), this kind-to-source table produces no candidates, so the promised path/directory completion is not implemented here; the test `test_none_path_dir_offer_nothing` explicitly locks in the empty result.

Given prefix `src/`, both calls return `[]` instead of matching paths or directories. The intent requires those sources, the module docstring lists `path` and `dir` as kinds this module answers, and `test_none_path_dir_offer_nothing` locks the empty result in so the missing completer cannot fail CI.

chunk_findings.detail: `kind == "state"` returns `CI.states(index=index)` and never applies `prefix`, unlike `kind`, `agent`, and `gate`, which go through `_prefixed`. Given states `["open", "closed"]` and prefix `"cl"`, `complete("state", "cl", index=index)` returns both names, so a partial word is offered choices that do not match it. The only test uses `prefix=""`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/values.py:complete

chunk_findings.detail: `_paths` builds the glob pattern by concatenating the raw completion prefix with `*` (`pat = prefix + "*"`) instead of treating the prefix as a literal filesystem path. Given a current directory containing both `a?.txt` and `ab.txt`, a completion request `V.complete("path", "a?")` uses the glob pattern `a?*`, so it returns `["a?.txt", "ab.txt"]`; `ab.txt` does not start with the literal prefix `a?` and is not a valid completion for that prefix. The same problem applies to prefixes containing `*` or `[` (e.g. a filename such as `[test].txt` can be treated as a glob character class), so `--repo`/`--globs` path completion can offer and insert the wrong filesystem path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/values.py:_paths

chunk_findings.detail: This test calls `os.chdir(tmp_path)` and never restores the working directory, nor does it use `monkeypatch.chdir`. After the test runs, the whole pytest process remains in that temporary directory. For example, a later test in the same session that calls `V.complete("path", "a")` outside this test will see the `a.txt` created here, and any later code relying on relative paths sees `tmp_path`, making the test suite order-dependent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_values.py:test_path_and_dir_complete_paths

chunk_findings.detail: `pat = prefix + "*"` is passed to `glob.glob` without `glob.escape`, so `*`, `?`, and `[` in the typed token are patterns, not a literal prefix. With files `ab.txt` and `a.txt` in cwd, `complete("path", "a?")` returns `["ab.txt"]` (and `complete("path", "*")` returns every non-dot name) even though none of those strings start with the prefix. Every other kind goes through `_prefixed` (`startswith`); these candidates do not, so TAB can insert a path the user did not type.

chunk_findings.detail: `os.chdir(tmp_path)` is never undone. After this test, process cwd is a pytest temp dir that is deleted at teardown. A later test that resolves a relative path, or any `getcwd()` once that directory is gone, fails or reads the wrong tree depending on order — the assertions only pass because they run before the leak matters.

chunk_findings.detail: `_paths` treats the completion prefix as a glob pattern instead of a literal path prefix: it globs `prefix + "*"` and never verifies that returned matches start with `prefix`. Given a literal filesystem path containing glob metacharacters, such as a file named `a[b].txt` (valid on Unix) and prefix `a[b]`, the pattern becomes `a[b]*`, which glob interprets as “`ab` followed by anything”.
